title: Add an object and move, rotate, scale it
summary: Add the Monkey head, then move it along one axis, rotate it by a set angle and scale it down.

steps.say: Check the top left of the 3D viewport. It should say Object Mode. If it says Edit Mode, press Tab.

checks.prompt: Does the mode selector at the top left of the 3D viewport read Object Mode?

hints: The mode selector is the first drop-down in the strip above the 3D view.
Click the selector and pick Object Mode from the list.
steps.why: Adding and arranging whole objects happens in Object Mode.

steps.say: With your mouse over the 3D viewport, press Shift A to open the Add menu.

checks.prompt: Is a menu titled Add open in the 3D viewport, listing Mesh, Curve, Light and Camera?

hints: Hold Shift, tap A, then let go of both.
You can also click Add in the viewport header.
steps.why: The Add menu holds every kind of object Blender can create.

steps.say: Point at Mesh, then click Monkey.

checks.prompt: Is there a new monkey head in the 3D viewport, highlighted with an orange outline, that was not there before?

hints: Mesh is the first entry. Its submenu opens to the side when you hover over it.
Or press F3, type Monkey, and press Enter.
steps.why: A new object always appears at the 3D cursor and is selected right away.

steps.say: Press G, then X, and move the mouse to slide the monkey along the red line. Click to confirm.

checks.prompt: Has the monkey head moved sideways away from the center of the grid compared to the start of this step?

hints: A red line appears after you press X. The monkey can only slide along it.
To move an exact amount, press G, X, type 2, and press Enter.
steps.why: Locking to one axis keeps the move precise and predictable.

steps.say: Press R, then Z, type 45, and press Enter to turn the monkey 45 degrees.

checks.prompt: Is the monkey head now facing a different direction than at the start of this step?

hints: The angle shows in the viewport header while you type.
Rotation is also in the sidebar. Press N and edit Rotation Z under Item.
steps.why: Typing a number gives an exact angle instead of guessing with the mouse.

steps.say: Press S, type 0.5, and press Enter to make the monkey half its size.

checks.prompt: Is the monkey head clearly smaller than it was at the start of this step?

hints: Type zero, a period, then five. The header shows the scale while you type.
Right click or press Escape to cancel, then try again. Control Z undoes a confirmed scale.
steps.why: Scaling with a typed value keeps the proportions exact.

steps.say: If anything looks wrong, press Control Z to undo it. Say done when the monkey looks right.
hints: Each Control Z steps back one action. Control Shift Z steps forward again.
steps.why: Undo makes it safe to experiment.
